terra.problem: The text does not say whether anyone was paying attention to the food.
Saying nobody was minding their own business adds a judgment about everyone present that the text does not give.
The man was before Jesus, but the text does not say he was standing or that he was in front of everybody.
The text does not say the man was standing.
The text does not say the healing happened at the table.
The text says Jesus sent the man on his way, not that he walked away.
The text does not say the man learned a lesson from being healed.
The line about the host's family needing a seat is a joke without a clear point.
A more distinguished guest being invited does not mean a fancier guest walks in after the person sits down.
The text does not say the more distinguished guest shows up after the person has taken the seat.
The text does not say everybody watches the person move to the last place.
The text calls the starting seat the place of honor; it does not say it is at the front.
The host tells the guest to move up; the text does not say the host moves the guest instead.
Being honored in front of everyone does not establish that nobody is looking at their plate.
Jesus says the people named may invite the host in return. The explanation adds that friends who show up and repay him are the problem.
The people who cannot repay the host are the guests Jesus tells him to invite, not necessarily everyone at the present table.
The guest says he bought the oxen, but not that he just bought them.
The text does not say the guest just bought the oxen or rule out a later sale.
The final sentence suggests that the named group is present at the actual dinner table. Jesus told the host to invite them, but the text does not say they were there.
The text does not say the highways and hedges are farther out than the streets and alleys.
The text does not explicitly say the highways and hedges are past the city streets.
The story does not say the original invitees' seats get filled by others or that the house is eventually filled.
